title: The Twin Ridge Burning Opposite

features.name: the mirror-burn
features.desc-on-touch: One ridge burns left-to-right; this one burns right-to-left. The fires will never meet. They teach each other through smoke and ash.

features.name: the ash-memory station
features.desc-on-touch: A tower of burned wood arranged to show both timelines of fire. Each log records a different burn pattern, a different teaching.

features.name: the convergent flame
features.desc-on-touch: Where both burns approach the summit but never arrive. The flame hesitates, unsure which way it was learned to burn.

features.name: the pattern-keeper
features.desc-on-touch: A carved marker showing both fire-paths. The burns around it are identical in inverse—as if the ridge is learning to burn both ways at once.

features.name: the ash-spread field
features.desc-on-touch: Gray matter from both burns settling into the same soil. The ash contains both fires' memories. It does not know which ridge it came from.

inscription: two ridges burning in opposite directions, each fire teaching the other how to burn the same pattern differently; the landscape learns from both at once

file.name: Burn_Pattern_Symmetry_Study_NSW_1994-2019.txt
file.note: Charred records comparing fire-fronts on facing ridges. The data shows a strange convergence: as years pass, the burn patterns grow more similar despite burning in opposite directions.
